summary: Comprehensive backend (pytest, 13 tests) and frontend (Playwright mobile viewport 375x667) testing completed for the Amazon Package OCR Scanner. All 13 backend tests PASS (health, settings GET/POST, sync 509 rows, orders list w/o _id, search by id+partial, lookup exact + fuzzy fallback for OCR confusion, lookup nonexistent, OCR with synthetic PNG containing real Order ID matched in DB, OCR no-id no-crash, empty sheet_url -> 400). Frontend: 4 tabs visible; SETTINGS shows the configured sheet URL, 509 total orders, status 'ok', SYNC NOW button works and refreshes last_sync_at; SEARCH instantly shows results for OD437102142031898100, tapping row opens ScanResultSheet bottom sheet with MATCH FOUND, customer, phone, product, amount, order date; Copy and Share buttons clickable with no permission errors; clear button works; HISTORY shows empty state with 'No scans yet. Start scanning packages.'; SCAN tab on web preview correctly shows 'Camera permission required' with GRANT ACCESS (expected web behavior). One transient OCR LLM failure (budget exceeded) occurred once and self-recovered; backend handles it gracefully (no crash). Console shows benign 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' RN-web warning; no red-screen errors. No deprecated Expo packages (expo-av/barcode-scanner/background-fetch) detected.

minor.issue: Intermittent LLM OCR failure observed once with 'litellm.BadRequestError: Budget has been exceeded'. Backend handles it safely (returns matched=false, no 500). Likely transient EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget/rate limit; consider exposing a clearer status in OcrOut so client can show a retry hint instead of 'no order id detected'.

issues: The Google Sheet contains two rows with the same order_id OD437102142031898100 (different customers Ngawang Jigme / Norzin Wangmo). Search shows both rows correctly, but the camera scan flow will silently pick the first match. Consider warning the operator when multiple matches exist for the same scanned ID.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Not from app code directly — likely from a dependency. Low priority; check whether it originates from react-native-safe-area-context / Modal / @expo/vector-icons usage.

action_items: Optional: surface a distinct 'OCR provider unavailable' state in OcrOut/UI so users understand transient EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget errors vs genuine 'no order id detected'.
Optional: in search results / ScanResultSheet, detect when more than one DB row shares the same order_id and show an ambiguity warning so operators can pick the correct customer.
Optional: investigate source of 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' RN-web warning (likely a transitive dep) — currently cosmetic only.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/orders/lookup fuzzy fallback only handles a single-character substitution from a fixed swap list; works as advertised but won't handle 2+ char OCR errors. Acceptable for v1.

Sync uses a delete_all + insert_all 'replace' strategy on every /api/sync. Safe for 509 rows but not atomic — a failed insert mid-way would leave the orders collection empty. Consider writing to a temp collection and renaming, or wrapping in a transaction.
OCR endpoint imports emergentintegrations lazily inside the handler each call — fine, but could be hoisted to module scope after first successful import to save a few ms per request.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data created. Used the user-provided Google Sheet (509 rows) which was already synced; synthetic PNG with the real order ID OD437102142031898100 was generated in-test for /api/ocr verification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend BASE_URL comes from env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. The test file uses Pillow to synthesize a real PNG (not solid color) containing the order ID text — keep this approach for /api/ocr tests per /app/image_testing.md. EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget can intermittently 'Budget has been exceeded'; a single rerun typically passes. Frontend tabs themselves do not have testIDs (Expo Router default tab bar) — use page.get_by_text('SCAN'|'SEARCH'|'HISTORY'|'SETTINGS', exact=True) to navigate.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. The single observed OCR test failure on first run was caused by an upstream LLM budget/rate-limit response (litellm BadRequestError 'Budget has been exceeded'); backend catches the exception and returns matched=false without crashing, and a retry passed.
